newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks inch higher in morning after weak start.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks inch higher in morning after weak start.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks inched up in morning trade on Monday, shrugging off early losses as property stocks began to recover after suffering over recent sessions from uncertainty surrounding the government's housing policy.
The Hang Seng Index was up 63.91 points, or 0.43 percent, at 14,886.88 after falling to an early low of 14,723.46. Turnover was HK$4.15 billion after the first 40 minutes of trade.

Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd recovered from an early low of HK$71.00 to trade up HK$0.75 at HK$72.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd gained HK$1.00 to HK$67.00 after hitting a low at HK$65.50.
"A lot of the property market uncertainty has already been reflected in the share prices," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
However, analysts expected a soft tone for property stocks in the near term until government policy on housing was clearer.
Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said last week that his administration may take measures to clamp down on property speculation and would increase housing supply.

"Unless there is more information about the actions the government will take in the future on property, there will not be much buying interest," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.

Red chips were the most heavily traded shares in morning trade. The red chip China-Affiliated Corporations Index was up 68.95 points, or 2.02 percent, at 3,486.38 with CNPC (Hong Kong) Ltd gaining HK$0.175 to HK$2.025 and China Merchants (Holdinhd) International Co Ltd up HK$0.55 at HK$23.60.
July Hang Seng Index futures were up 15 points at 14,845.
